newsitem.title: USA: Montgomery Cty, Md., seeks more school aid - paper.
newsitem.headline: Montgomery Cty, Md., seeks more school aid - paper.

text.p: Montgomery County, Md., County Executive Douglas Duncan said he plans to ask the state for a large boost in school contruction aid, the Washington Post reported Wednesday.

Montgomery County received $38 million in aid last year, but Gov. Parris Glendening has said that amount might be too high. Duncan, in contrast, said the county is entitled to $70 million, and he would ask for that amount in next year's budget.

Glendening sparked controversy among some local officials when he proposed increasing Prince George's County's budget by $90 million to $250 million in special aid. Earlier this year, Baltimore County won a package of $254 million over five years in new state school aid.
Duncan has asked for a statewide approach to allocating funds, rather than a county-by-county competition.
